title: 10 Ways Sales Leaders Use Chloe Chat to Manage their Team
summary: Ten Chloe Chat prompts sales leaders use to coach from real calls, spot why deals win, measure speed-to-lead, and walk into 1:1s and forecast meetings prepared.
body_markdown:
I talk to sales leaders all day, and every one of them has a list of questions they’d love to dig into and no time to do it. What do we actually do on the deals we win? How long do leads really wait? Which reps are hunters and which are closers? The answers are buried in hundreds of calls and email threads, so the list keeps growing.


[Chloe Chat](https://close.com/blog/meet-chloe-chat-your-personal-assistant-built-into-close) , the AI assistant built into Close, changes that. Ask a question, and Chloe works through the calls, emails, notes, and pipeline history already in Close CRM, then comes back with specifics you can act on.


Here are the Chloe Chat prompts I rely on most: the ones that finally crack questions I could never get to, and the ones that handle jobs that used to eat up most of my week.


### 1. Coach from real calls


You can’t coach a conversation you never heard, and nobody running a team has time to listen to every call.


Chloe Chat works from your call recordings and Notetaker transcripts to pull out the moments worth a[sales coaching](https://close.com/blog/sales-coaching) conversation: how a rep handled pricing, whether they set a clear next step, and which objections keep coming up.


**Prompt:**


*Review \[rep name\]’s recorded calls and meetings from the past week. Tell me first how many had transcripts available. Then summarize:*


- *The objections prospects raised and how \[rep name\] responded*
- *Calls that ended with no agreed next step and date*
- *One moment that went especially well and one worth coaching on, with the call each came from*
- *A pattern I should raise in our next 1:1*


*Keep it focused on specific moments, not a general grade.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, help me coach my calls](https://close.com/links/ry6r)


**Why it matters:** Every piece of feedback points back to a specific call, so the conversation stays on facts.


*Pro Tip: Calls only have transcripts if recording and transcription are turned on, so the count tells you whether you’re seeing the whole week or half of it.*


### 2. Find out why you win


When you lose a deal, everybody wants to know why, and the reason goes in a report. When you win one, you celebrate, the deal leaves the pipeline, and the reason it closed leaves with it. But the move you actually want your whole team repeating lives in the win.


**Prompt:**


*Review the opportunities my team won in the past 90 days in \[pipeline name\]. Group them by won reason. For each of the top 3, pull the specific moment from the call or email thread where the deal turned, quote it, and tell me what the rep did. Flag any example where the evidence shows the buyer had already decided rather than something the rep created.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, show me why we won these deals](https://close.com/links/tuzb)


**Why it matters:** Your team learns exactly what worked on the deals you won.


### 3. See how fast your team really responds


Most speed-to-lead reports count an automated email as a response. Your buyer doesn’t. From their side, the clock keeps running until a real person reaches out.


Measure your team’s speed-to-lead rate from the buyer’s side, and you get two numbers back: how quickly your team typically follows up, and how many new leads never heard from anyone at all.


**Prompt:**


*For leads created in the past 30 days, calculate the time from lead creation to the first outreach by a human rep, excluding automated workflow email, shared-team accounts, and AI agent activity. Show median and 90th percentile per rep and by hour of day. Count leads with no human outreach separately rather than as zero, and tell me what share that is.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, measure how fast we respond to leads](https://close.com/links/k473)


**Why it matters:** You’ll know whether your team needs to move faster or just make sure every lead gets worked.


### 4. Spot your hunters and your closers


Win rate tells you how often a rep closes. It doesn’t tell you what they started with. Some reps are hunters who build deals from cold outreach. Others are closers who turn warm, interested leads into customers. Both can post the same numbers while doing very different work.


This prompt tells them apart by looking back at how each opportunity was created. For every deal a rep opened, it checks the lead’s status at that moment, so you can see whether the rep started from a warm lead or a cold one.


**Prompt:**


*For every opportunity \[rep names\] created in the past 90 days, reconstruct what the lead’s status was at the moment the opportunity was created, not its status now. Group by the rep who created it. Tell me which reps are converting leads that were already warm versus creating opportunities from cold or untouched leads, and each rep’s win rate on each type. Exclude open deals from the win rate.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, show me what kinds of leads my team is closing](https://close.com/links/nn7a) .


**Why it matters:** Hunters and closers need different coaching, and now you’ll know which one each rep needs.


### 5. Check in on team activity


Activity isn’t the whole story, but it’s usually where a problem shows up first. If a rep’s calls dropped off two weeks ago, there’s probably a reason, and you want to have that conversation now, not at the end of the quarter.


Chloe can pull the numbers behind the[sales KPIs](https://close.com/blog/sales-kpis-metrics) you already track and compare each rep against their own recent baseline. That way a change stands out instead of hiding in a team total.


**Prompt:**


*Build a table of activity for each rep on my team over the past 2 weeks: calls made, connected calls, emails sent, meetings held, and new opportunities created. Compare each rep to their own average over the previous 6 weeks, and flag anyone whose activity changed by more than 25% in either direction.*


**Try it now:[C](https://close.com/links/d5n6)**[hloe, check in on my team’s activity](https://close.com/links/d5n6)


**Why it matters:** You catch the dip, or the breakout week, while you can still do something about it.


### 6. Walk into every 1:1 prepared


A good 1:1 is about the rep’s deals and development, not 15 minutes of status updates. Let Chloe handle the status part before you sit down.


**Prompt** :


*Prepare me for my 1:1 with \[rep name\]. Review their open opportunities, their activity over the past 2 weeks, deals they won or lost this month, and any deals with no activity in 10+ days. Create a short note with:*


- *What’s going well, with specifics*
- *Deals that look stuck, and why*
- *Changes in their activity*
- *3 questions I should ask*


*Keep it skimmable enough to review in 2 minutes.*


Tr **y it now:**[Chloe, prep me for my 1:1](https://close.com/links/262e)


**Why it matters:** The conversation opens on the real issues, not on catching up.


### 7. Get the forecast meeting ready


Tamina, one of our reps,[cleans up her pipeline](https://close.com/blog/8-ways-chloe-chat-saves-me-admin-work) every Tuesday before our forecast meeting using Chloe. Chloe can also do the manager’s pass across everyone’s deals. That way, your[pipeline review meeting](https://close.com/blog/sales-pipeline-review-meeting) starts with the risks already on the table instead of uncovering them one rep at a time.


**Prompt:**


*Review open opportunities in \[pipeline name\] owned by \[rep names\] that are expected to close this quarter. Flag:*


- *Expected close dates that have already passed*
- *Deals with no call, meeting, or rep-sent email in the past 14 days, excluding automated and workflow emails*
- *Deals where the most recent conversation contradicts the recorded stage or amount*


*Group the results by rep, summarize the total value at risk, and show me the evidence behind each conversation flag. Don’t change anything. I’ll review these with each rep.*


**Try it n** ow:[Chloe, get my forecast meeting ready](https://close.com/links/https://close.com/links/cv4pcv4p)


**Why it matters:** You walk into the meeting knowing which deals are at risk, so the time goes to fixing them.


### 8. Hand off deals without losing the thread


Reps take vacations, change territories, and sometimes move on. The prospect shouldn’t be able to tell.


Whether it’s two weeks out of office or a permanent[rep offboarding](https://close.com/blog/offboard-sales-rep) , the hard part is capturing what lives in the rep’s head before they go.


**Prompt:**


*\[Rep name\] is out starting \[date\]. Review their open opportunities and add a .handoff note to each Lead page with where the deal stands, the last conversation and anything that was promised, open questions or risks, and the next step with a date. Then give me a summary table of all their deals, ranked by value and urgency, so I can reassign them.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, write handoff notes for my rep’s deals](https://close.com/links/wa7j)


**Why it matters:** Whoever takes over the deal picks up right where the last conversation left off.


### 9. Get new reps up to speed faster


New reps have a lot of questions about the product, the process, and the accounts they just inherited. Not all of them need to wait for a spot on your calendar.


Chloe can answer account questions from the lead history and how-to questions from the Close Help Center. That takes some of the load off your[new sales hire onboarding](https://close.com/blog/how-to-onboard-new-sales-hires) .


**Prompt for the new rep:**


*Summarize everything that’s happened with \[Lead name\]: past conversations, what they care about, open questions, and what I should know before I call them.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, catch me up on this lead](https://close.com/links/5bca)


**Prompt for you:**


*Compare \[new rep name\]’s first 30 days of activity and pipeline with the rest of the team. Tell me where they’re ahead, where they need help, and what I should focus on in our next 1:1.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, show me how my new rep is ramping](https://close.com/links/y2m6)


**Why it matters:** New reps get answers when they need them, and you know where to spend your coaching time.


### 10. Get reports instantly


Most of my questions about a team are easy to ask and annoying to answer. Where did last quarter’s pipeline come from? Which channel actually turns into meetings? Answering usually means building a report, exporting it, and counting.


With Chloe Chat, you ask the question and get the answer back as a table, often with a chart.


**Prompt:**


*Show me where our new leads came from over the past 6 months, grouped by lead source. For each source, include the number of leads, how many reached a qualified or meeting-booked stage, and the conversion rate between the two. Show the results as a table and a chart, and call out the biggest changes from month to month.*


**Try it now:**[Chloe, show me where my leads come from](https://close.com/links/wvcy)


**Why it matters:** When the answer takes seconds instead of hours, you actually ask the question.


*Pro Tip: tell Chloe who you mean. Most teams have groups in the CRM that aren’t the sales team, and “my team” will quietly pull in onboarding, support, and anyone else who happened to hold a meeting. Name the pipeline or name the reps, and the answer gets a lot sharper.*


#### More time for the part only you can do


Chloe can show you that a rep’s calls dropped or a deal hasn’t moved in three weeks, and every answer comes from your own Close data: your team’s real calls, emails, and deals. Deciding what to do about it, and how to have that conversation, is still your job. Chloe handles the digging, so more of your week goes to your reps and the deals that need you.


Start with one question you’d normally spend an hour answering. Open Chat in Close or **press ⌘J (Ctrl+J on Windows)** and ask it this week.
